POLLUTANTS                                        Conc        Conc.      Aquatic      Supply       Aquatic       Health       Criteria   Criteria       Criteria   Criteria   Criteria   Criteria
                               CAS No.     MQL   Ca (ug/l)   Ce (ug/l)   2.13*Ce   Cd,dom (ug/l)   Cd (ug/l)   Cd,hh (ug/l)     ug/l       ug/l          ug/l        ug/l       ug/l       ug/l
candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel criteria columns (domestic supply, irrigation, livestock/wildlife, acute aquatic, chronic aquatic, human health) plus instream waste-concentration derivations from effluent (Ce). Which column or derivation path is treated as the enforceable discharge limit, and whether MQL/Ca/Ce govern comparability, changes limit selection (A), which parameters are in monitoring scope (B), and how blank or derived fields are classified when evidence is incomplete (C).

This heading groups calculated instream concentrations (2.13*Ce, Cd,dom, Cd, Cd,hh) that sit alongside standalone numeric criteria. Interpreting these as operative limits versus intermediate modeling outputs changes which numeric value is compared to reported measurements (A) and whether missing Ca/Ce or zero modeled instream values represent resolved no-comparison states versus unresolved inputs (C).

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table column header (lines 10-11)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Need TMDL column header is split across header rows (Need on the upper row, TMDL on the lower). Whether this column signals that TMDL-based limits are absent, not applicable, or must be sought elsewhere changes whether a numeric criteria value in the table is the sole enforceable limit or whether applicability remains open for TMDL-driven limits.

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table (all pollutant rows)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Every listed pollutant shows N/A in the Need TMDL column. Interpreting N/A as confirming no TMDL limit applies versus leaving TMDL limit status unresolved changes whether table criteria alone govern compliance comparison.

Many criteria cells use the sentinel 1E+100 rather than a finite limit. Treating this as no enforceable numeric limit (report-only or non-comparable) versus a literal numeric ceiling changes whether measurements require compliance comparison (A) and whether missing results for those parameters are classified as non-applicable monitoring versus unresolved expectations (C).

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table row Phenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row shows blank ambient (Ca) and effluent (Ce) inputs, zero modeled instream concentrations, a finite domestic criterion (10500 ug/l), 1E+100 aquatic criteria, and a finite human-health criterion (860000). Different choices about which column applies, whether zeros reflect documented no-discharge modeling, and whether blank Ca/Ce block limit derivation change limit applicability and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table row Pentachlorophenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: This pollutant carries multiple finite criteria (domestic 1, acute aquatic 19, chronic aquatic 15, human health 30) alongside MQL 50. Selecting acute versus chronic aquatic criteria, or domestic versus human-health endpoints, changes the enforceable limit (A). The stated MQL also affects whether monitoring/reporting at or above that level is required for this parameter (B).

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table row Benzidine
candidates.computation_change_reason: Extremely low domestic (0.0015 ug/l) and human-health (0.002 ug/l) criteria paired with MQL 50 create ambiguity about whether reported values below MQL can be compared to these limits, whether monitoring is effectively required at detection levels far below MQL, and how non-detect or missing results should be classified relative to such stringent criteria.

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table row Nonylphenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: Unlike other pollutants in the segment, Nonylphenol has no stated MQL and blank Ca/Ce fields, while still listing finite acute (28) and chronic (6.6) aquatic criteria. Whether monitoring/reporting thresholds default when MQL is unstated, and whether aquatic limits apply without effluent modeling inputs, changes monitoring obligation resolution (B), limit selection (A), and how missing quantification/reporting evidence is categorized (C).

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table subsection header
candidates.computation_change_reason: This grouping label separates base/neutral extractable pollutants from prior phenolic compounds in the table. Interpreting it as defining a distinct monitoring analyte group or study scope changes which parameters are considered required for the facilities covered by this reasonable-potential analysis.

candidates.locator: Page 6, section body, table (all pollutant rows, instream columns)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Every pollutant row shows zeros in the instream waste-concentration columns (2.13*Ce, Cd,dom, Cd, Cd,hh). Interpreting these as modeled zero-discharge/no-instream-loading assumptions versus placeholders affects whether instream-derived limits are operative for comparison (A) and whether the zeros document a no-discharge/no-data state or leave modeled inputs unresolved (C).
